bounded_statement: The selected result claims an occurrence rate for the entire scheduled survey network (96 scheduled stations) but computes it as 18/72 using only the screen-retained subset as the exposure denominator, excluding the 24 screened-out scheduled stations from the denominator; the complete-domain denominator entailed by the stated task and the report's own target population is 96, so the reported 0.25 overstates the complete-network rate relative to the 18/96 = 0.1875 complete-domain computation.

counterevidence_considered.description: Falsification probe: the report transparently discloses the retained/omitted counts and names the 72-station denominator, which might be read as an explicitly conditional target; however the disclosure is only descriptive accounting and the selected claim and stated target population remain the entire 96-station scheduled network, and the report states no method deviation was approved, so transparency does not convert the claim into a subset-conditional one.
counterevidence_considered.observed_value: denominator disclosed but claim scope unchanged; no approved deviation

evidence.description: Row-level data show the 24 excluded stations are scheduled units (scheduled=yes) that were merely screened out, so they belong to the complete scheduled domain the claim covers.

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I tried to falsify the issue by looking for any statement that makes the target explicitly conditional on passing the signal screen, which would place the case outside scope. task.md L0001 asks for a rate 'for the entire scheduled survey network'; results/report.md L0004 states the target population as 'all 96 scheduled coastal stations'; and the selected-result line itself is labelled 'for the entire scheduled survey network'. No conditional-on-screen framing exists anywhere. I next tried to falsify the arithmetic premise by checking whether the excluded 24 rows might be out-of-domain (unscheduled) units; every omitted row in inputs/data.csv carries scheduled=yes, so they are inside the claimed domain. Finally I checked whether a complete-domain rate was reported elsewhere in the report and found none, and results/report.md L0018 confirms no approved deviation licenses the subset denominator. The mismatch survives all three attempts.

root_cause: The workflow hard-codes the retained-subset count SCREEN_PASSED_STATIONS = 72 as the exposure denominator in the selected-result line while labelling that quantity a rate 'for the entire scheduled survey network', so the 24 screen-omitted but scheduled stations are dropped from the exposure base rather than retained with zero observed occurrences.
